question: Can a sequence-to-sequence transformer generate all renormalizable particle-physics Lagrangian terms permitted by SU(3) x SU(2) x U(1) field content and learn the underlying symmetry concepts?

key_findings.claim: A specialized object-and-contraction tokenization lets BART generate symmetry-respecting symbolic Lagrangians with high in-distribution exactness.
key_findings.evidence: On roughly 64,000 held-out generated cases, sampled- and uniform-data models achieve perfect Lagrangian scores on 92.0% and 93.2%; object and contraction exactness are higher, showing most misses concern term completeness.

key_findings.claim: The model extrapolates syntactically to more fields but loses gauge conservation and completeness as contextual counting grows.
key_findings.evidence: For seven to ten fields, over 99% of outputs remain structurally reasonable, while U(1) conservation drops from 89.5% to 86.8%; error analysis shows missing terms, mixed field quantum numbers, and a seven-to-eight-field tracking limit.

key_findings.claim: Embedding probes are consistent with learned group representations and conjugation, but do not establish a symbolic algorithm.
key_findings.evidence: The encoder clusters fields by SU(2)/SU(3) representations and maps conjugate pairs to related directions; dummy-index renaming in outputs also suggests invariance beyond memorized strings.

method.core_idea: Encode particle fields, representations, operators, and explicit index contractions as a finite vocabulary and train BART from field lists to complete Lagrangian sequences.
method.mechanism: A symbolic generator enumerates valid training targets; separate sampled and uniform data distributions expose term/length tradeoffs, while an encoder-decoder transformer learns conditional sequence generation with cross-entropy.
assumptions: The training generator correctly enumerates all target terms.
The restricted field types, gauge groups, mass dimensions, and no-repeated-field setting cover the evaluation domain.
Sequence metrics canonicalize irrelevant term and dummy-index orderings correctly.

techniques.role: Makes fields, representations, operators, and contractions explicit to the transformer.
Produces exact supervised pairs across controlled field distributions.
Separates correct objects, contractions, missing terms, and extra terms.

evaluations.result: Perfect Lagrangian score is 92.0% sampled and 93.2% uniform on the merged test set.

evaluations.metric: Reasonableness, U(1) conservation, and term score
evaluations.result: Reasonableness stays above 99%; U(1) conservation falls to about 87% and term omissions increase.

evaluations.setting: Standard Model and BSM examples plus representation probes
evaluations.result: Many known models are reconstructed and embeddings group by quantum representation.
evaluations.baseline: Ground-truth generated Lagrangians and labeled representation relations

limitations: Training targets come from an exact symbolic generator, so learned generation does not yet replace the source algorithm.
The study excludes repeated flavors/groups, vector fields, higher-dimensional EFT operators, and continuous couplings.
Context length and counting failures cause missing terms in larger field sets.
failure_modes: The decoder omits combinatorial terms as the number of fields increases.
Field quantum numbers are mixed when the encoder cannot isolate repeated FIELD regions.
Unusual rational U(1) charges expose weak numerical token representations.
reusable_insights: Scientific sequence models need semantics-aware scoring that factors object, relation, contraction, and completeness errors.
Program-generated corpora are most informative when extrapolation axes are withheld explicitly.
Embedding geometry is useful hypothesis evidence but should be paired with causal or symbolic consistency tests.
open_questions: Can constrained decoding guarantee gauge invariance and term completeness while letting the model rank plausible theories?
Does training on repeated flavors and EFT bases produce compositional rather than enumerative scaling?
Can a model propose novel field content under experimental constraints rather than reproduce generator outputs?

competitive_landscape.title: SYMBA: Symbolic Computation of Squared Amplitudes in High Energy Physics with Machine Learning
competitive_landscape.difference: SYMBA maps interaction descriptions to squared amplitudes; this work maps field content to the full allowed Lagrangian and explicitly scores gauge contractions.

competitive_landscape.title: Transforming the Bootstrap: Using Transformers to Compute Scattering Amplitudes in Planar N = 4 Super Yang-Mills Theory
competitive_landscape.difference: Cai et al. predict exact amplitude coefficients in a fixed theory; the Lagrangian model generates interaction terms across varying particle content and Standard Model gauge representations.

competitive_landscape.title: Learning the Simplicity of Scattering Amplitudes
competitive_landscape.difference: Cheung et al. simplify algebraically equivalent spinor-helicity expressions; this paper constructs invariant terms from quantum-number specifications.

novelty_assessment: Reviewer inference: transformers had already performed symbolic mathematics and amplitude calculation. The novel task formulation is conditional generation of gauge-invariant Lagrangians from particle content with contraction-aware tokenization, OOD field-count tests, and representation analysis.
reviewer_notes: Full methods, data generation, metrics, in/OOD experiments, embedding discussion, appendices, and conclusion were checked. High accuracy is within a generator-defined restricted theory space. Primary records checked 2026-08-23.
